title: Three Junes and One Short Gown
subtitle: 毕业升学 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 毕业升学（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：毕业升学（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：graduate　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 graduate 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the dean ① praised a graduate that no examiner in the hall would have described, and he said the praising was the whole of the June. The ② graduate, meaning the student himself and not the class, ran three Junes and stayed undescribed in the book; a graduate, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ graduate in that hall had the same short gown beside it, and the ④ graduate at the far row, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A graduate, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the dean said the describing is the part that fills three Junes.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the graduate was the whole of the matter, meaning the degree and not the student. The ⑥ graduate, meaning the degree and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; graduate, he said, is either something you praise or the only word that means both a student and a degree. He said the degree is the part they remember.

By 1984 the ⑦ graduate had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short gown. The ⑧ graduate of the whole thing, the dean wrote in November, was one hall and three Junes of describing; graduate, he said, is either the one at the far row or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ graduate I remember is the one described in the list, which closed in 1986 and is still described as the quietest in the hall. A ⑩ graduate, my mother said in 1988, is the only one that improves by being described; every graduate, she said, is a degree that has agreed to look like a student. She said the degree was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 毕业生（指大厅里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 毕业生（指那个学生本人，与班级相对）
C. 固定搭配：praise a graduate 称赞一位毕业生
D. n. 毕业生（指留给孩子们学的那一位）
E. n. 毕业（抽象总称，指一处大厅的毕业之事）
F. n. 毕业生（指名册里写到、被记下的那一位）
G. n. 学位获得者（指一件事里人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 学位（抽象总称，指人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: praised a graduate that no examiner in the hall would have described
The graduate, meaning the student himself and not the class
the graduate at the far row
the graduate was the whole of the matter

answers.why: praise a graduate 意为“称赞一位毕业生”，1979 年那位院长称赞了大厅里没有一位考官肯描述的一位毕业生。
graduate 意为“毕业生”，指那个学生本人而不是班级，它经过了三个六月而在簿子上没有被描述。
graduate 意为“毕业生”，指大厅里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一件矮矮的学位服。
graduate 意为“毕业生”，指最远那排留给孩子们学的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
graduate 意为“学位获得者”，指一件事里人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位学位获得者就是那件事的全部。
graduate 意为“学位”，指人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位毕业生，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
graduate 意为“毕业生”，指名册里写到、被记下的那一位，到 1984 年这一位成了名册里的一行。
graduate 意为“毕业”，院长十一月写道，整件事的毕业之事是一处大厅和三个六月的描述。
graduate 意为“毕业生”，我记得的是名册里描述过的那一位，1986 年毕业了，至今仍被说成大厅里最安静的一位。
graduate 为抽象总称，母亲 1988 年说，一位毕业生是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的东西。
